claims.text: A combinatorial synthesis approach can create compositionally graded thin films of HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy.
Compositionally graded HfNbTaTiZr thin films allow the roles of individual elemental variations in mechanical properties to be identified.
Even small changes in the elemental percentages of HfNbTaTiZr significantly affect hardness.
Even small changes in the elemental percentages of HfNbTaTiZr significantly affect elastic modulus.
Controlled deposition techniques such as sputtering can systematically vary the percentage of one or more elements across an HfNbTaTiZr thin-film sample.
Variations in elemental percentages induce changes in local phase formation.
Variations in elemental percentages induce lattice distortions.
Changing elemental percentages alters lattice parameters.
Changing elemental percentages alters defect density.
Composition-induced changes in lattice parameters and defect density modulate solid-solution strengthening.
Changes in solid-solution strengthening are reflected in local mechanical properties.
Regions with altered contents of specific elements will exhibit statistically significant differences in nanoindentation hardness relative to the nominal composition.
Regions with altered contents of specific elements will exhibit statistically significant differences in elastic modulus relative to the nominal composition.
Results obtained from thin films and laboratory-scale mechanical tests may not directly extrapolate to bulk materials or alternative processing routes.
Scale-dependent phenomena and differences in deposition cooling rates may affect translation of the observed behavior to bulk alloys.
